payload.description:
## Trigger

When the focused time/token changes have landed in a release candidate, I want to compare that exact candidate with the baseline through real consumer journeys, so I can accept a demonstrated saving instead of an isolated microbenchmark.

## Required proof

Reuse the same small bug fix, docs change, clean consumer install/upgrade and two-lane journey defined by basicly-h79lott.3. Record end-to-end elapsed time, phase/check durations, duplicate check execution, permission/repair/cleanup interventions and actual token/context usage where the host exposes it. Mark unavailable CPU or billing data as unavailable. Warm and cold conditions must be named, and the exact commit, package hash, check inputs and runtime versions recorded. Reuse valid evidence for the same artifact rather than rerunning by habit. Exercise foreign hooks/configuration, staged-versus-working content, changed inputs and failed cleanup/confirmation controls. Do not claim repository-size scaling or cross-host savings from this limited matrix.

## Approval boundary

This is planning and release acceptance only. Implementation, new dependencies, CI edits, release publication and paid probes require their applicable approvals. Agree numerical time/token budgets after the baseline, before optimization is accepted.

- When a native ship challenge is immediately answered with its printed code, the loop shall approve the checkpoint without replacing the outstanding code first.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an approved native ship retry receives the immediately preceding confirmation code, I want that code to remain valid until consumption or expiry, so I can finish normal work without repeated permission failures.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the pinned pre-change wheel and drive an ordinary manual task through its confirmed change and successful merge.
2. Capture the ship challenge printed by loop run, then immediately run the offered command with its code.
3. Observe ship REFUSED with invalid or expired confirm code, although no human or time delay changed the challenge. All four lanes in the measurement reproduced this.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_policy_confirm_store.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Evidence

loop._on_verify calls approve_checkpoint_guarded with no code before run_ceremony consumes the supplied code. The no-code path issues and replaces the current ship code. Native command evidence and the installed package identity are preserved in native-confirmation-reproduction-v1. This defect directly blocks the agreed baseline and release consumer journeys; its bounded correction is covered by the user pre-approval of everything connected to this goal.

payload.description:
## Context

Decided by the orchestrator, 2026-11-12: the removal of the old ledger files after a cutover is outside the M5 core. Deleting files from a code repository stays with the owner. In the core (basicly-gtb19bg.43.22) the old ledger stays in place, frozen, with a MOVED.md marker.

## Acceptance

- A named removal step shall delete the old ledger files only when fsck --code shows that no open branch in the code repository still carries lines that are not in the vault. Branches in forks are out of reach; the step shall print that it cannot see them.
- Proof T-ledger-removal: input a cut-over fixture with one open branch holding an unimported line; action the removal step, then migrate --branch on that branch, then the removal step again; pass when the first run refuses by branch name and the second removes the files.
- When a branch that changes a removed ledger file is found after the removal step, migrate --branch shall import its lines by event id and remove its ledger changes so that the branch merges with no conflict, and fsck --code shall import such lines from any branch that lands.
- When the removal step runs, fsck --code shall fetch every branch on the code remote, list each branch that is not merged and carries ledger lines not in the vault, refuse by branch name if any exist, print that fork branches and branches never pushed cannot be seen, and delete the files in one commit only if the default branch head has not moved since the check.
- Proof T-ledger-removal-remote: input a cut-over fixture whose unimported line is only on a remote branch that has no local copy, and a second branch that appends to a shard after removal; action the removal step, then merge the second branch after migrate --branch; pass when the first run refuses by the remote branch name and the merge has no conflict.
payload.title: Remove the frozen ledger files after a vault cutover

payload.description:
## Context

Owner question, 2026-08-22: *"I also understand that the only things that are shown on the board are the ones started by supervisor. what about other subagents or background agents - are they also shown on the board?"*

The answer is **no**, and it is structural rather than an omission in the producer.

## Measured

A board lane comes from one place: `board_facts.lane_facts` calls `supervise.derive_session(...)` and reads `state.adopted` (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:237-238`). An `AdoptedLane` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:466-474`) is *"one in-flight lane re-adopted from its br worktree binding"* and carries a required `loop_state.WorktreeBinding`.

So a thing appears on the board if and only if it has **a tracker record carrying a `worktree:` external_ref**. A subagent spawned through a host's own agent tool has neither. A background shell job has neither.

`rg -n 'subagent|sub-agent|background|spawn' src/basicly/board_*.py` returns two hits and both are prose in unrelated docstrings, saying the producer *spawns* nothing. Positive control: `rg -c 'lane' src/basicly/board_facts.py` returns 30, so the probe reaches the files and the absence is real.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The region is headed `RUNNING NOW`. A reader takes that as *what is happening in this repository*, and on 2026-08-22 the true answer included four read-only investigation subagents and two background shell jobs that the board could not see and did not mention. The heading over-claims: it means *what the supervisor dispatched*, and nothing says so.

That is the same class as `basicly-a68ggd`, where a region headed `THE LOOP` shows the whole backlog. A heading that names more than its producer can see is a defect whichever direction the gap runs.

## What is genuinely hard here

A subagent is **not** a lane and should not be drawn as one. It has no tracker record, no worktree, no branch, no acceptance criteria, and no landing. Giving it a lane card would invite a reader to expect a merge that will never come.

It also may not be observable at all. A lane is a subprocess this engine spawned and metered, so its stream is readable; a subagent of the *host* is inside the host's own process tree and the engine has no handle on it. Whether it can be counted at all is the first question this record has to answer rather than assume - and if the answer is that it cannot, then the honest fix is the heading and not a new section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN work is running that the board cannot see, THE PAGE SHALL NOT imply it is showing everything, and the region's heading SHALL name the population it actually draws.
- WHEN it is established whether a host subagent or a background job is observable by this engine at all, THAT FINDING SHALL be recorded with its evidence, because the design depends on it and it is currently unknown.
- WHERE such work is observable and shown, IT SHALL be visually distinct from a lane and SHALL NOT carry a lane's affordances, since it has no branch and no landing.
- WHERE it is not observable, THE HEADING FIX ALONE SHALL be the deliverable, and the record SHALL say so rather than leaving a section stubbed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-ibzr0f`
- demonstration: Run a supervised pass while separately running work the engine did not dispatch, then read the board and check that nothing on it claims to be showing that second population - and if the design admits it, that it is drawn as something other than a lane.
payload.title: running now names more than the board can see so undispatched work is invisible without saying so

The five undrawn are basicly-3iaw0x (deferred), basicly-mfavrh (merged on main, record never advanced), basicly-85cadb, basicly-jt0dgi and basicly-tjhjmk (worktree bound, no dispatch, other roots). The board said nothing about any of them. Breakdown recorded on basicly-a68ggd.

[measured 2026-09-05, from reading the board] This record's heading fix has a second half that is sharper than 'name the population': the note currently gives a WRONG CAUSE for the region's own emptiness.

Drawn on the live page:

    RUNNING NOW   waits on a blocker - 56 record(s) have an unmet dependency

Read plainly that says nothing is running BECAUSE 56 records are blocked. The same page prints READY 231, so blockers are not the reason and cannot be. The real reason is four lines up in small grey type, in the loop region's note: 'no pass is running'.

So the hero region answers a question nobody asked, with a figure that does not bear on it, while the true answer is drawn elsewhere in the smallest text on the page. A reader who trusts the note concludes the factory is dependency-starved when it is simply not running.

The heading fix this record already asks for should carry it: when no pass is running, say that, and say it here rather than under the diagram. The blocked count belongs in the footer beside BLOCKED 56, where it already is.

Filed alongside: basicly-5jkxqk, which is the other half of the same emptiness - IN PROGRESS 1 is counted three times on the page and never named.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When work is running that the board's `running now` region cannot see, I want the region to name only the population it actually draws, so I can trust it will not imply it is showing everything.

## Context

Owner question, 2026-08-22: *"I also understand that the only things that are shown on the board are the ones started by supervisor. what about other subagents or background agents - are they also shown on the board?"*

The answer is **no**, and it is structural rather than an omission in the producer.

## Measured

A board lane comes from one place: `board_facts.lane_facts` calls `supervise.derive_session(...)` and reads `state.adopted` (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:237-238`). An `AdoptedLane` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:466-474`) is *"one in-flight lane re-adopted from its br worktree binding"* and carries a required `loop_state.WorktreeBinding`.

So a thing appears on the board if and only if it has **a tracker record carrying a `worktree:` external_ref**. A subagent spawned through a host's own agent tool has neither. A background shell job has neither.

`rg -n 'subagent|sub-agent|background|spawn' src/basicly/board_*.py` returns two hits and both are prose in unrelated docstrings, saying the producer *spawns* nothing. Positive control: `rg -c 'lane' src/basicly/board_facts.py` returns 30, so the probe reaches the files and the absence is real.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The region is headed `RUNNING NOW`. A reader takes that as *what is happening in this repository*, and on 2026-08-22 the true answer included four read-only investigation subagents and two background shell jobs that the board could not see and did not mention. The heading over-claims: it means *what the supervisor dispatched*, and nothing says so.

That is the same class as `basicly-a68ggd`, where a region headed `THE LOOP` shows the whole backlog. A heading that names more than its producer can see is a defect whichever direction the gap runs.

## What is genuinely hard here

A subagent is **not** a lane and should not be drawn as one. It has no tracker record, no worktree, no branch, no acceptance criteria, and no landing. Giving it a lane card would invite a reader to expect a merge that will never come.

It also may not be observable at all. A lane is a subprocess this engine spawned and metered, so its stream is readable; a subagent of the *host* is inside the host's own process tree and the engine has no handle on it. Whether it can be counted at all is the first question this record has to answer rather than assume - and if the answer is that it cannot, then the honest fix is the heading and not a new section.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-ibzr0f`
- demonstration: Run a supervised pass while separately running work the engine did not dispatch, then read the board and check that nothing on it claims to be showing that second population - and if the design admits it, that it is drawn as something other than a lane.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run any agent without the supervisor - a bare claude session in this checkout, or `basicly loop run` before its worktree binds - then open the board: the lanes region names only records carrying a worktree external_ref, and `running now` counts more work than any visible lane, with nothing on the page saying the difference exists.

payload.description:
Field incident shipping basicly-yzyd.1: running 'basicly loop advance' with cwd inside a loop worktree (not the base checkout) made the merge fail ('merge must run from the base checkout ... currently on harness/<name>') yet the ship-checkpoint approval and teardown still proceeded, leaving the child CLOSED but UNMERGED with its commit stranded on the harness branch. The engine should detect it is running from a linked worktree (or that 'main' is not the checked-out base) and refuse the merge/ship transition with a clear error, instead of approving-and-stranding. Also: worktree cleanup --force did not remove the orphaned .git/basicly-worktrees/<name>.json session record once the branch was already deleted, and that stale record counts toward the worktree concurrency cap. Recovery used: git rebase main harness/<name> + git merge --ff-only + git branch -d + rm the stale session json.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a leaf worktree via the loop and cd into it (the linked worktree)
2. From inside the worktree, run 'basicly loop advance <id>' at the build or ship phase
3. Observe the merge fail on base-checkout assertion while ship approval/teardown still closes the bead, stranding the commit on harness/<name>

## Acceptance Criteria

* loop advance refuses the build and ship transitions when run from a linked worktree (git-dir != git-common-dir), returning a graceful blocked result that names the base checkout and mutates no tracker/worktree state
* worktree cleanup drops the session record when the branch is already gone, so no orphaned .json counts toward the concurrency cap
* regression tests cover the linked-worktree refusal and the already-deleted-branch cleanup
payload.title: loop advance from a linked worktree should refuse the merge/ship transition

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while landing basicly-m0p1, which edits `.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py`. The
build->verify landing failed with `projection-hooks`:

    Stale hook projection detected. Run `basicly hooks-build` to sync hooks.
      .basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py: differs from catalog

The projection was not stale. `hooks.check_hooks` compares `_catalog_hooks_dir()` - the hooks
directory of the **installed** basicly package - against `repo_root / core_hooks_dir`, and skips the
comparison entirely when the two resolve to the same path. In this repo basicly is installed editable
from the base checkout, so `_catalog_hooks_dir()` resolves to
`<base><redacted:posix-absolute-path>`. The loop's landing verify runs with `repo_root` set to the **lane's
worktree**. So the check compares the pre-merge BASE copy against the post-change WORKTREE copy and
reports a difference that is the change itself.

Measured: base copy md5 `97d34d0e...`, worktree copy md5 `389ad855...`, and calling
`check_hooks(<worktree>, Path(".basicly/core/hooks"))` from the base interpreter reproduces the single
mismatch exactly.

Consequence: **any change to a hook script is unlandable through the loop.** It is not "landed by its
own pre-merge version" (the documented `merge.py`/`loop.py`/`verify.py` trap) - it structurally cannot
pass, and it consumes the rework budget on each attempt (observed at 1/2 after one try).

**The dangerous part, and the reason this is P1 rather than an annoyance:** the failure message tells
the operator to run `basicly hooks-build`. In a worktree that copies the base's OLD script over the
new one, silently reverting the work while turning the gate green. An agent following the message
faithfully destroys the change and reports success.

Note the check is only meaningful for a CONSUMER repo, where `.basicly/core/` is materialised from the
wheel and can genuinely drift. In the dev repo `src` and `dst` are the same directory, so the content
comparison is skipped and the gate has no signal to give - which is why it passes from base and fails
only from a worktree.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Provision a worktree for any bead and edit any file under `.basicly/core/hooks/`.
- Commit it on the harness branch, then run `basicly loop run <id> --root <id>` from base.
- Observed: `projection-hooks` fails naming the edited script as differing from catalog, the merge is
  rolled back, and rework increments. Expected: the check compares like with like - or is skipped -
  when the repo under verification is a linked worktree of the checkout the package is installed from.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a harness worktree whose hook source differs from the base checkout it was branched from when
  the landing verify runs the projection-hooks check then the check does not report the change itself
  as drift and the landing proceeds, and given a consumer repo whose materialised hooks genuinely
  differ from the installed catalog then it still fails, and the failure message no longer advises a
  command that would revert the change when run in a worktree, with tests
payload.title: A hook script change cannot pass the landing verify from a worktree

policy.py:226        _ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_SECTION in body     substring anywhere
plan_record.py:66    has_heading                              a stripped line equal to the heading

description contains the heading as inline prose

- `tests/test_plan_record.py`

payload.description:
tests/test_integration_wait.py asserted 'waited_s <= _WAITED_S + _SLACK_S' with _SLACK_S=5. The fixture pins policy._now to time.time()+600, so the recorded interval is 600 plus however long the two real br round-trips take. The upper bound therefore budgeted five seconds for two subprocess invocations.

On a loaded full-suite run (15m37s wall) they took nine, producing 'assert 609 <= (600 + 5)' and failing the pre-push gate for a defect that did not exist. Three test_integration_dor_scaffold setup errors in the same run were xdist contention, not real - that file passes 15/15 in 40s on its own.

Fixed by taking the overhead from time.monotonic() around the two calls and allowing it explicitly, per .claude/rules/platform-hermetic-tests.md ('wait for the condition, never for a duration'). The bound keeps its power: with ~1s elapsed the ceiling is ~606s, so a mis-zoned stamp hours off still fails.

Found while pinning br to 0.2.16 (basicly-o7z5); unrelated to that change.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-21. `basicly-rn0o.4` blocked `basicly-rn0o.3` while `basicly-rn0o.4`'s own `## Plan` section declared it depends on `basicly-rn0o.3`. The renderer was therefore the one board lane no supervised pass could dispatch, and nothing reported the disagreement.

Two sources hold one fact. `plan_record.parse_plan_section` reads the declaration off the body; the `edge` events hold the graph. The decomposer writes both from one plan, so they agree at creation and can drift on any later hand edit or `dep add`.

Measured over the whole tracker with a positive control: 231 open records, 22 carry a `- depends on:` line, 313 live `blocks` edges, and the declared set is a subset of the edges on 19 of the 22. Two of the three misses declare by title rather than by id, which the title-keyed plan graph accepts at decompose time. One was the inverted edge.

## Why this is a gate and not a note

An inverted edge reads as correct from either side. The record says one thing, the ready set says another, and an operator reading the record believes the lane is dispatchable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a records `- depends on:` line names an id that is not one of its live `blocks` edge targets, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero and name the record, the declared id and the edges it does have.
- WHEN a declaration names a title rather than an id, THE CHECK SHALL resolve it against the titles in the tracker before reporting a miss.
- WHEN every open record agrees, THE CHECK SHALL exit zero and print the reconciled count and the population it covered.
- WHEN no open record carries a depends-on line at all, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero, because an empty population is the probe failing rather than the tree passing.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_declared_dependencies.py`
- `tests/test_check_declared_dependencies.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_declared_dependencies.py` printing the reconciled count, and exit 1 after a deliberate `dep remove` of one declared edge.
payload.title: reconcile a records declared depends on against the blocks edges it actually has

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given every line of the always-on baseline when it is audited then each line records whether a hook could enforce it and whether a glob could scope it and whether it changes behaviour versus the default and the no-op lines are named for removal
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 4 step 1. Depends on 1a for its urgency.

Audit every baseline line against three questions:
- is this really a hook - can a git hook or a verify check enforce it instead of asking;
- can I write a glob for it - does it belong in the path-scoped tier rather than always-on;
- does it change behaviour versus the default at all.

Expect all three to fire. The third is the no-op test and the plan calls it the single most common defect in an always-on layer: a rule that restates what the model would do anyway costs context on every turn and delivers nothing.

Measured starting point 2026-07-26 at c175c1a: 7014/7209/7343 chars across AGENTS.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md, about 1070 words each.
payload.title: Audit every always-on line for hook glob and no-op

payload.text:
A checkable predicate for this audit, 2026-08-08, from a five-source review of CLAUDE.md authoring guidance. The bead asked 'does this line change behaviour versus the default?' and had no way to answer it. Two thirds of that is now mechanical:

1. Already enforced by a hook, linter, formatter or CI gate? -> DELETE, point at the gate. Mechanically checkable: grep the rule's subject against .pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml, basicly.toml [[verify.checks]]. The repo's own quality-gate fragment already says 'Point at gates, don't restate them' - this applies that rule to the always-on file itself.
2. Derivable from a config the agent can read (pyproject.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml)? -> DELETE. Mechanically checkable.
3. Restates default model behaviour? -> DELETE. NOT mechanically checkable, and no source in the review supplied a method beyond 'run some tasks and observe whether the rule is followed'. This is still the open half.

Evidence quality of the review, stated because it bounds how much weight to give the above: FIVE sources, ZERO measurements. No A/B, no adherence rate, no n, no method anywhere. Three sources gave three incompatible size ranges (40-80 lines, 50-300 lines) against the vendor's 'under 200', none with a method. One source's whole token-cost argument rests on 'CLAUDE.md is prepended to every Claude turn', which contradicts the vendor mechanism (delivered once as a user message after the system prompt) - so its sizing advice is unfounded. Two of the five sell a product whose premise is their own recommendation.

Also settled while reviewing, and it removes a risk rather than adding work: one source claimed Claude Code auto-loads AGENTS.md, which would mean every consumer of  double-loads ~22k chars since we project BOTH .claude/CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Measured against a live session's own context: the repo has AGENTS.md at root, the context lists two CLAUDE.md files by path, and AGENTS.md is absent from that list. A differential, not an empty probe - the announcing mechanism demonstrably works. No double-load on the installed version. /context is the authoritative check and needs a human to run it.

Unused new idea, recorded not adopted: counting IMPERATIVES rather than characters or lines as the size unit. Cited as '150-200 instructions before compliance drops' with no citation, no study, no link. Do not gate on it; at most report it beside the existing counters.

SHARPENED PREDICATE, 2026-08-08: 'enforced for one family is not enforced'.

Predicate 1 says 'already enforced by a gate -> delete, point at the gate'. That is true ONLY PER AGENT FAMILY, and this repo projects to three. Worked example on require-explicit-confirmation, measured against .claude/settings.json permissions.deny (25 rules):

    HARD-DENIED on claude   rm -rf (4 variants); git push --force/-f/--force-with-lease;
                            push|commit --no-verify/--no-gpg-sign; git reset --hard;
                            git clean -f; filter-branch/filter-repo; .env read+edit
    PROSE ONLY              git checkout -- <path>; git restore; git stash; rebase

4 of 7 items are strictly weaker as prose than the deny-list already enforcing them, so predicate 1 would delete the section. It must not:

1. The 3 commands with NO deny rule (checkout --, restore, stash) are exactly the ones the fragment's second bullet enumerates, because nothing blocks them and each discards uncommitted work irreversibly.
2. Copilot and Codex have no config-level deny at all. Copilot gets --deny-tool only when OUR runner dispatches (basicly-lqz5); a human typing copilot gets nothing. For those families the prose is the whole control.

RULE: before deleting a line under predicate 1, name the enforcing mechanism FOR EACH projected family. Delete only when all are covered; otherwise keep it and make it say which families it is load-bearing for.

Deliberately NOT adding a per-item table of what claude denies: permissions.yaml changes and a table rots, while the fragment's generic sentence ('covers only some of these and varies by agent') stays true and was verified accurate.

AUDIT RUN 2026-08-09. The headline is that this bead's premise is wrong: the always-on layer is not
what puts AGENTS.md over its cap, and evicting from it would damage three families to fix one
family's problem while leaving the cause untouched.

## Measured

  .claude/CLAUDE.md                8628 / 9000    372 UNDER
  .github/copilot-instructions.md  8727 / 9000    273 UNDER
  AGENTS.md (codex)               13550 / 12000  1550 OVER

  always-on body, 20 fragments     8462 chars   -> all three families
  scoped body, 3 fragments         5091 chars   -> AGENTS.md ONLY

Confirmed by differential rather than by inference: `Platform-Hermetic`, `PureWindowsPath` and the
external-review text each appear once in AGENTS.md and zero times in the other two.

## Cause

claude.yaml and copilot.yaml set `exclude_scoped: true` and receive the scoped tier as separate
`.claude/rules/*.md` files carrying `paths:`. codex.yaml does not set it, because codex has no
glob-based instruction scoping and never loads a nested AGENTS.md below the cwd. So codex must
inline the whole scoped tier into its always-on file. 8462 + 5091 = 13553, which is AGENTS.md.

The overage is therefore structural to codex, not a symptom of an accreted baseline.

## Predicates 1 and 2, run anyway because they have value independent of the overage

Predicate 1, a gate already enforces it: 8 of 20 fragments name a subject found in
.pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml, basicly.toml or pyproject.toml - require-explicit-confirmation,
quality-gate, commands, core-rules, secure-coding, git-discipline, catalog-authoring,
project-defaults. Those 8 total 4057 chars.

**None of them is deletable on that basis**, and the sharpened predicate already recorded on this
bead is why: every one of those gates is a git hook or a lint run, which fires at COMMIT time, after
the tokens that produced the violation are already spent. That is the same argument factory-loop
section 11 item 8 now makes. require-explicit-confirmation is the worked example the earlier comment
already settled - 4 of its 7 items have no deny rule on any family, and copilot and codex have no
config-level deny at all.

Predicate 2, a glob could scope it: 5 of 20 name a path token (commands, project-overview,
copilot-defaults, claude-defaults, project-defaults). Scoping any of them helps claude and copilot,
which are already under cap, and moves the text INTO codex's inlined tier - making AGENTS.md worse,
not better. Predicate 2 is actively counterproductive here and that is a property of the projection,
not of the lines.

Predicate 3, the no-op test, remains the open half. No source in the 2026-08-08 five-source review
supplied a method beyond running tasks and observing, and basicly-agzx.1 is the bead that would
measure it.

## What this bead should become

Not an eviction. The decision is how codex carries a tier it cannot scope, and the options are
recorded for the owner: raise codex's cap toward its real budget (project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB
default - 12000 was our conservative pick, not the vendor's limit); or set exclude_scoped on codex
and accept that codex gets no test-discipline, external-review or tier-routing guidance at all; or
build a per-fragment opt-out so only some scoped fragments inline.

payload.description:
D36, decided 2026-08-09. Supersedes basicly-a3ab.9's D35 half, which assumed paths was a front
matter line it is not.

## Why a fence rather than a top-level key

schemas/skill.schema.json carries exactly the Agent Skills portable subset - name, description,
license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools - with additionalProperties false. That is
deliberate: a projected SKILL.md is meant to be portable to any host. `paths:` is outside the subset
and is claude-only. A top-level key makes every shipped skill unportable to buy one behaviour.

## Scope

- `claude:` (or per-target) object in skill.schema.json holding host-specific keys.
- skills.py `_optional_frontmatter` emits fenced keys only into the roots that understand them:
  .agents/skills gets the portable six, .claude/skills gets six plus fenced.
- `paths: ["**/*.py"]` on python-guidelines under the fence.
- agent.schema.json already establishes this shape - follow it rather than inventing a second one.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` green; .claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md
carries the paths key and .agents/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md does not; touching a .py file in
a fresh session loads the skill without it being named.

## Constraint

D25 - catalog guidance, human approves the diff.

payload.description:
Measured 2026-08-09 by the gate basicly-u2hl.45 shipped, and it fires today:

  skill listing is 2081 tokens against a 2000-token budget
  (1% of claude's 200000 adapter-default window), from 31 model-invoked entries

## Why this is a consumer defect and not a local one

basicly.toml raises this repo's claude window to 1000000, so locally the listing sits at ~21% of
budget and looks fine. A fresh `basicly install` inherits the 200000 adapter default and is over.
The overrun is therefore invisible to anyone measuring here, which is how it went unnoticed.

## Why it compounds

The host drops descriptions starting with the LEAST-INVOKED skills. 8 of 34 were ever exercised when
that was last measured. So the entries this overrun silences are the ones already hardest to reach,
and silencing them makes them harder still.

## The remedy is authoring, not code

Options, in the order that costs least:
- Move a skill to `invocation: user`. A user-invoked entry carries no description and contributes
  only its name - that is the saving the invocation axis exists to buy, and it is now asserted by a
  test.
- Retire a skill nothing invokes. The usage telemetry (`basicly usage`) is the input.
- Shorten the longest descriptions. harness-loop 509, python-guidelines 458, wsl 408, python 392.

81 tokens is the overrun. One user-invoked move is likely enough.

## Constraint

D25 - catalog content, so the diff goes to a human. Do not retire a skill on a zero-usage reading
alone without checking whether it was ever reachable: an entry whose description was already being
truncated is not evidence of a skill nobody wants.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly catalog lint` emits no listing-budget warning.
payload.title: Bring the skill listing under the budget a consumer actually gets

payload.text:
Done. Measured 2026-08-09 in base.

The bead's figure was stale: it recorded 81 tokens over from 31 entries. Reproduced today the
overrun was 342 over from 34 entries, because the three loop skills authored for basicly-4kdm
(decompose-plan 101, validate-as-consumer 88, repair-in-place 71 = 260 tokens) landed after it
was filed. One user-invoked move could never have covered that.

Cut taken (owner's call, D25): the 15 remaining model-invoked tool-* skills move to
invocation: user, keeping tool-br (used=7). This finishes a split that already existed - six
tool-* skills (tool-bat, tool-fzf, tool-git-delta, tool-starship, tool-wezterm, tool-zsh) were
already user-invoked. All 15 had zero recorded invocations over the whole telemetry history.

  listing  2342 -> 1696 tokens against a 2000 budget   headroom 304
  entries    34 -> 19 model-invoked

Larger than a field flip, for the next reader: routing_evals.py:99 refuses an evals.yaml owned
by a non-model-invoked slug and :116 refuses a negative naming one as owner, and
skill_source refuses a description on a user-invoked entry. So it was 15 invocation flips + 15
description deletions + 15 evals.yaml deletions + 9 negative-case rewrites in skills that stay
model-invoked (node, python, wsl, interface-facts x2, conventional-commits, tool-br,
worktree-isolation, harness-client, test-discipline).

No routing quality was lost: rank-1 rate held at exactly 88.9% across the change (80/90 ->
40/45, floor 85.0%), so the removed positives were hitting rank-1 at the same rate as the rest.

Verified: catalog lint OK with no listing-budget warning; basicly check / skills-check
--all-default-roots / agents-check / hooks-check / permissions-check all up to date; pytest
3604 passed; ruff check + format clean. Confirmed on the live consumer surface too - the

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When the investigation runs, it shall establish a reproducible cold and warm release baseline and account for elapsed time, agent coordination, available token/tool costs, repeated checks, setup, packaging, hooks, pushes, CI queue/runtime and publication waits, with unknown quantities marked unavailable.
- When a delay is assigned a cause, the research shall cite the actual instruction or call path and demonstrate the causal mechanism or clearly label the remaining hypothesis. It shall distinguish required independent safety controls from redundant work over equivalent trusted inputs.
- When the baseline is established, the task shall record a measurable improvement target and implement the smallest supported changes, including canonical release guidance or orchestration when they cause the delay. A report alone shall not complete this task.
- When the improved process is tested, the actual final tagged candidate, release notes, install pins, uploaded artifacts and fresh consumer behavior shall remain verified. Dirty user work, canonical release ownership, immutable published tags, failure recovery and existing genuine approvals shall remain protected. No gate, test, check, cap or hook shall be weakened or bypassed, and no execution witness shall be fabricated.
- When before and after results are compared, they shall use comparable release cases and report complete elapsed time, sample size and limits. Moving work outside the measured interval or after publication shall not count as an improvement. The result shall demonstrate the recorded speed target while preserving safety.
- When changes affect tracker handling or telemetry, historical events shall remain append-only and independent tracker PRs shall still merge in either order without manual tracker conflict resolution or a main-into-branch merge required solely by tracker file changes. Prefer leaving the existing schema and Git merge behavior unchanged; exercise both merge orders if they change.

## Trigger

When cutting a verified release still takes substantial elapsed time and repeated coordination, I want to investigate the complete release path and implement the demonstrated improvements, so I can publish safely with less wall time and agent effort.

## Context

## Trigger

When PR #1 reports failures that our checks did not expose, I want an independent investigation of its claims and proposed changes, so I can decide whether they are valid, explain any coverage gap, and choose the appropriate PR response.

## Filing scope

Only file this story now. Do not investigate validity, implement changes, update the branch, comment on the PR, merge it or close it until the user selects this work. Keep the PR open and unchanged during filing.

## PR snapshot

URL: https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/pull/1
Title: fix(hooks): make hooks work on windows and scope no-comments to added lines
Head: fix/windows-hooks at a89e8f5f64394e5f745afd616539ddf8b9022bf7
Base: main
State at filing: OPEN

The description reports consumer problems on Windows 11 with Git Bash, uv 0.9.5, Store Python 3.12 on PATH and an existing Python 3.12 virtual environment. Its baseline is basicly v0.26.11. These are the author's claims, not findings established by this filing. Compare that baseline, the PR head and current main; re-fetch the current head and discussion before investigating.

## Claims to inventory and assess

- Text subprocess decoding in hooks reportedly fails on UTF-8 diffs under a Windows legacy code page and can surface a secondary identity-guard exception. Assess both the decoding failure and the safety of replacement decoding.
- Staged snapshots reportedly copy large environment directories when symlinks lack privileges, hit long-path failures and isolate usage writes. Assess the proposed junction fallback, target-preserving cleanup and failure behavior.
- Repository-relative check programs reportedly resolve incorrectly on Windows in normal execution and fix paths. Trace every affected caller and verify both platform path forms.
- The no-comments hook reportedly rejects existing comments in edited files despite wording about new additions. Assess the proposed added-line filter, new/untracked files, staged snapshots, renames and multiline docstrings. Separate a demonstrated defect from a proposed policy change; do not silently weaken the approved comment ban.
- Hook launchers reportedly select Python 3.12 despite the engine's Python requirement. Assess interpreter selection, existing consumer environments, the proposed fixed 3.14 request, standalone-kit compatibility, and the reported Lefthook Windows quoting/redirection behavior.
- Inventory the reported pre-existing Windows test failures separately, including foreign hook arguments/execution, initial commits and staged fixes, consumer exclusions, progress timing and other named install/upgrade cases. Check their relevance to accepting this PR rather than assuming the branch introduced or fixes them.
- Assess the smaller observations about terse hook errors, UV_NO_SYNC with no-project, imported identity fields and scrub, same-version wheel caches, and the reported isolated-versus-parallel comments-kit test behavior. Verify the PR's regression and end-to-end testing claims independently.

## Required research

Read the complete current description, issue and review comments, inline threads and every changed file. Map each claim to a reproducible case, actual call sites, current requirements and controls. Use native Windows consumer evidence for Windows-specific mechanisms, plus deterministic cross-platform controls where possible. Establish what remains unverified if native evidence is unavailable.

Explain why each confirmed issue escaped: missing platform coverage, fixtures that miss the consumer condition, insufficient assertions, instruction/policy ambiguity, environment assumptions, drift since the baseline or another demonstrated cause. Distinguish causation from correlation and a claimed test from proof that the condition was live.

After the evidence, recommend one disposition with reasons: merge as proposed, request/update specific changes, comment with findings or clarification, or decline/close. Separate technical validity from whether the proposed solution is safe and appropriate. Obtain any required concrete approval before an external PR action; this filing authorizes none.

- UTF-8 hook subprocess decoding: Confirmed on baseline and original main. Fixed UTF-8 subprocess boundaries and child encoding; scanner failures remain failures.

- Same-version local wheel is stale until --no-cache: Current uv did not reproduce same-version wheel staleness. The older uv 0.9.5 environment remains unverified. Latest installers resolve an immutable versioned release wheel.
- Comments-kit whole-tree test is timing-sensitive: The reported comments-kit parallel failure was not reproduced. Its timing cause remains unknown; no flake-resolution claim is made.
- All added tests fail before the fix; verification and consumer end-to-end: The claim that every added test failed before the fix was overstated. Added discriminating native controls, real commits, refusal checks and fresh/upgrade wheel checks.
